text: Imagine breathing through a straw that keeps getting thinner. That is what an asthma attack can feel like. Around two hundred and sixty million people live with asthma. So what is actually happening inside their airways?

Asthma is a long term disease of the airways, the bronchi and bronchioles that carry air into the lungs. In asthma, these airways are inflamed and extra sensitive, so they overreact to things that don't bother other people.

During an asthma attack, three things happen at once. The muscles around the airways squeeze tight. The lining swells up. And the airways fill with thick, sticky mucus. Together, they make the airway much narrower.
Air has to squeeze through a narrow pipe, especially when breathing out. That makes the whistling sound called a wheeze. Air also gets trapped in the lungs, which makes the chest feel tight.
The main signs are wheezing, coughing, often at night or early morning, a tight chest, and shortness of breath. They can come and go, and they can be mild or severe.
Attacks are often set off by triggers. Common ones are dust mites, pollen, pet hair, mold, smoke, air pollution, cold air, exercise, colds and flu, and strong smells.
To diagnose asthma, doctors listen to the chest and use a breathing test called spirometry, which measures how much air you can blow out, and how fast. A peak flow meter can track it at home.

Treatment usually means two kinds of inhaler. A reliever opens the airways within minutes during symptoms, by relaxing the tight muscles. A preventer, used every day, calms the inflammation so attacks happen less often.

Get emergency help if breathing is very hard, if someone can't speak in full sentences, if their lips or fingernails turn blue or grey, or if the reliever isn't helping. Call your local emergency number.

So remember. In asthma, sensitive airways squeeze, swell, and fill with mucus. Know your triggers, use a preventer to stay well, and a reliever for quick help. Asthma can't be cured, but it can be controlled. Next, we'll look at pneumonia, an infection deep in the lungs.
